sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Let's explore how static members work in Java - they're like shared tools for all objects of a class!

• What static variables, constants, and methods are
• How they differ from instance members
• When and how to use them effectively

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine a classroom with a whiteboard. The whiteboard is 'static' - everyone in the class can see and use it. That's exactly how static members work in Java!

Static members belong to the class itself, not individual objects. Here's what that means:

• **Static Variables**: Shared across all instances (like the classroom whiteboard)
- Declared with `static` keyword
- Only one copy exists for the entire class

• **Constants**: Special static variables that never change
- Declared with `final static`
- Named in ALL_CAPS_WITH_UNDERSCORES
- Example: `final static double PI = 3.14159;`

• **Static Methods**: Class-level functions
- Can be called without creating an object
- Example: `Math.sqrt(25)` (no Math object needed!)

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ Static members belong to the class, not objects
✓ Only one copy exists for static variables (shared)
✓ Constants are `final static` and named in ALL_CAPS
✓ Static methods can be called without objects

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Use static for shared configuration values
Use static methods for utility functions
donts: Don't overuse static - it breaks OOP principles
Don't modify static variables from instance methods
sections.protip: Static members are great for memory efficiency - they prevent duplicate data across objects!

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Where you'll see static members in real applications:

examples.how: Java's Math class uses static methods (Math.sqrt(), Math.PI) so you don't need to create Math objects
Apps use static constants for settings like MAX_USERS or DEFAULT_TIMEOUT that apply everywhere
Static variables track total objects created or total operations performed across all instances

problem.description:
Create a Circle class with:
1. A static constant PI (3.14159)
2. A static method to calculate area (PI * radius²)
3. An instance variable for radius
4. An instance method to get circumference (2 * PI * radius)
hints: Remember: static methods can't access instance variables
Use ClassName.staticMethod() to call static methods
problem.explanation: The static PI constant is shared by all circles. The static calculateArea() method works without a Circle object, while getCircumference() needs an instance to access the radius.

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Static members belong to the class, not objects
📌 Constants are `final static` and named in ALL_CAPS
📌 Practice using static for shared data and utility methods
📌 Ready to learn about visibility modifiers next!
